h: קוּנְטְרֵס עֲמֵלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, ד׳ Kuntres Amalah Shel Torah, 4

p: which is the bread of poverty,
engenders poverty and lowliness in the heart;
and this is a preparation for receiving the Torah,
for they leave a high place
and go to a low place
the more the words of Torah descend there.
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who was more humble than any man,
merited receiving the Torah from Hashem,
and that it is called by his name.
and Torah they will seek from his mouth, etc." —
for he said, "And what are we?"
And Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
the two thousand years of Torah —
And Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
we call it Torah she'b'al peh" —
"Not because you are more numerous, etc.,
for you are the fewest, etc." —
they were chosen as the portion
"And with the crushed and lowly of spirit
he becomes a vessel to receive
the words of the Written Torah,
which is the power of "the Torah of Hashem,"
which is called "the Torah of your mother";
fear of Heaven falls upon him,
through the revelation of His Shechinah, Yisbarach,
this is the revelation of the Shechinah";
for through the revelation of the Shechinah
great awe falls upon a person.
"The reward of humility is the fear of Hashem."
for entering the gates of Torah,
"The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem."
that this is why they instituted
two cups before eating the matzah
For every fear of some thing
that some harm will reach him,
Not so the fear of Hashem:
it is stated in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah
and rejoiced out of my fear";
which he recognizes through his joy;
And likewise, out of the fear —
the light of the revelation of His Shechinah, Yisbarach,
Therefore we drink wine, which gladdens,
And all of it is preparation for receiving the Torah.
And in the Torah too there are both,
for it is called "The fear of Hashem is pure, etc.,"
and "The precepts, etc., gladden the heart" —
for it engenders joy and fear in the heart.
And such is the way of Torah:
in the manner of a poor man
as they said at the beginning of Berachos
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן הֲכָנָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
And this too is a preparation for the words of Torah:
to accustom oneself to the bread of poverty,
but to make do with little.
And he eats in the manner of freedom,
for there is no free man
except one who toils in Torah,
for he is happy with his portion
draws down an abundance of blessing
As they said in Bereishis Rabbah (84:17)
on the pasuk "And they sat down to eat bread,"
that their eating brought bread to the world,
which was drawn down on their account
For the eating of the Tribes of Hashem
and with an abundance of holiness;
all the more so the eating of matzah,
over which we recite the blessing
"Who has sanctified us with His mitzvos and commanded us" —
for it is an eating that places holiness
in the heart of those who eat it,
an abundance of livelihood and sustenance
